title: Manzie Campbell, Collier's Shows and the Eko and Iko act
summary: He praises Manzie Campbell as the greatest drummer, who could roll perfectly with his left hand, and describes the sideshow of Collier's Shows.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: by the name of Manzie Campbell. I forgot that I met Mr. Manzie Campbell with the Collier Shows; the greatest show that you had that toured nowhere but in the South was Mr. Collier's Show. Mr. Collier had two daughters who was very light-skinned and they said, "Limabeans from New Orleans." But that wasn't the name of the show... which you know the name of the show...
What was this gentleman Mancy like?

Manzie Campbell was the only man that I have ever seen or met, or anybody ever met in the world, that could take his left hand and play a perfect drum roll. The show that he was on - I had met him - was a silent screen show. You must remember in those days when P. G. Lowry was playing the side show - this was before the Ubangi tribe because the only attraction they had was Eko and Iko. They were two albinos that when one would say one thing, the other would repeat. "How's the weather today?" "How's the weather today?" "It's going to rain today." "It's going to rain today." And that was a 25¢ addition to the side show.
